The test image shows a sugarcane leaf with a broad pale/yellow stripe along the midrib region, and a dark brown elongated lesion centered within that pale area. The surrounding leaf tissue is green. This mid-rib yellowing pattern is characteristic of Yellow Leaf disease.

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The Yellow Leaf reference shows widespread whole-leaf yellowing/browning across entire leaves, which doesn't match the test image. 

Re-analyzing the test image more carefully:
- A single elongated dark brown lesion
- Surrounded by a broad pale/yellow halo zone
- Otherwise green leaf tissue

This pattern (dark brown oval lesion with yellow halo) is the classic hallmark of **Brown Spot** disease, not Yellow Leaf (which causes diffuse whole-leaf yellowing). The reference Yellow Leaf image confirmed they are whole-plant/whole-leaf yellowing, not localized lesions with halos.

This lesion-with-halo pattern is characteristic of Brown Spot disease. Yellow Leaf (confirmed by reference) shows whole-leaf yellowing, not discrete lesions. Leaf Scald produces pencil-line cream stripes rather than discrete oval lesions with halos."}
